Kairat''' ({{langx|kk|«Қайрат» футбол клубы|«Qairat» futbol kluby}}) is a professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Almaty]], which plays in the [[Kazakhstan Premier League]], the highest level of [[Football in Kazakhstan|Kazakh football]]. Founded in 1954 as Lokomotiv Alma-Ata, they became Urozhay in 1955 and Kairat in 1956. The club's home ground is the [[Central Stadium (Almaty)|Central Stadium]] which has a capacity of 23,804 seats. The club's home kit colours are yellow and black striped shirts, black shorts and black socks. Kairat was the leading Kazakh club during the Soviet period and the only representative of the [[Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic]] in the [[Soviet Top League]].{{Cite web|website=[[UEFA]]|author=Aidyn Kozhakhmetov|script-title=ru:"Кайрат": пять поводов для гордости|trans-title="Kairat": five reasons for pride|language=ru|url=https://ru.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0223-0e912f2b30cd-c0c2d6b82fd0-1000--%D0%BA%D0%B0%D0%B8%D1%80%D0%B0%D1%82-/|date=8 July 2015|access-date=8 September 2017|archive-date=26 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190726135522/https://ru.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid%3D2263988.html|url-status=live}} For this, Kairat became nicknamed ''The Nation's Team'', and remains widely supported all over the country.{{Cite web|website=sports.kz|script-title=ru:Кайрат Боранбаев: Кайрат — Народная команда. Так было всегда, и мы хотим это возродить|trans-title=Kairat Boranbayev: Kairat is the People's Team. It has always been so, and we want to revive it|language=ru|url=https://www.sports.kz/news/kayrat-boranbaev-kayrat-narodnaya-komanda-tak-byilo-vsegda-i-myi-hotim-eto-vozrodit/comment/1213957|date=3 March 2015|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=2 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221102130913/https://www.sports.kz/news/kayrat-boranbaev-kayrat-narodnaya-komanda-tak-byilo-vsegda-i-myi-hotim-eto-vozrodit/comment/1213957|url-status=live}} All in all, the club spent 24 seasons in the Soviet highest level. They also won [[Soviet First League]] titles twice, in 1976 and 1983. During this period, Kairat was a part of the [[Voluntary Sports Societies of the Soviet Union]]. In modern history, Kairat won five [[Kazakhstan Premier League|league]] titles, eight [[Kazakhstan Cup]]s and two [[Kazakhstan Super Cup]]s. The club's strongest rivalry is [[FC Astana]], among fans their matches are considered as the Two Capitals Derby.{{Cite web|publisher=Football Federation of Astana (FFA)|title=Two Capitals Derby: Astana Share Spoils With Kairat Thanks to Last-Gasp Equaliser|url=https://sportsffa.kz/kazakhstan-football/171212308-astana-kairat-share-spoils-2017-kpl-season-match-report/|author=Tlek Adryshev|date=2 May 2017|access-date=6 September 2017|archive-date=6 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906180708/https://sportsffa.kz/kazakhstan-football/171212308-astana-kairat-share-spoils-2017-kpl-season-match-report/|url-status=dead}} == History == === Founding === The club was founded in 1954 as ''Lokomotiv Alma-Ata'' on the basis of the football club [[FC Dinamo Alma-Ata|Dinamo Alma-Ata]].{{Cite web|author=Asema Tungishbayeva|work=BNews.kz|script-title=ru:Архивные документы ФК «Кайрат» впервые показали общественности|trans-title=Archival documents of FC "Kairat" were first shown to the public|language=ru|url=https://bnews.kz/ru/news/sport/arhivnie_dokumenti_fk_kairat_vpervie_pokazali_obshchestvennosti_foto-2015_11_26-1196533|date=26 November 2015|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=28 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151128032107/http://bnews.kz/ru/news/sport/arhivnie_dokumenti_fk_kairat_vpervie_pokazali_obshchestvennosti_foto-2015_11_26-1196533|url-status=dead}} Heretofore, Dinamo was developed by [[Nikolai Starostin]], who is mostly known as "the father of Soviet football" and founder of the [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]].{{cite news|author=Alexander Weinstein|newspaper=[[Sovetsky Sport]]|script-title=ru:Николай Петрович Старостин. Он по-прежнему всё видит...|trans-title=Nikolai Petrovich Starostin. He still sees everything ...|language=ru|url=http://www.sovsport.ru/blogs/blog/bmessage-item/6841|date=17 February 2003|access-date=7 September 2017|archive-date=8 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908024117/http://www.sovsport.ru/blogs/blog/bmessage-item/6841|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|work=Caravan|script-title=ru:Легендарный Старостин. Годы ссылки в Алма-Ате|trans-title=Legendary Starostin. Years of exile in Alma-Ata|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/sport/legendarnyjj-starostin-gody-ssylki-v-almaate-102262/|date=28 March 2003|access-date=7 September 2017|archive-date=8 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908021109/https://www.caravan.kz/sport/legendarnyjj-starostin-gody-ssylki-v-almaate-102262/|url-status=live}} His assistant Arkady Khokhman became the first head coach of the club.{{Cite web|publisher=Semyon Neverov|website=footballfacts.ru|script-title=ru:Николай Старостин в Казахстане|trans-title=Nikolai Starostin in Kazakhstan|language=ru|url=http://footballfacts.ru/articles/148194-nikolaj-starostin-v-kazahstane|access-date=7 September 2017|archive-date=26 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200126124400/http://footballfacts.ru/articles/148194-nikolaj-starostin-v-kazahstane|url-status=dead}} Lokomotiv joined Zone I of the [[Soviet First League|Class B]], the second tier of Soviet football. In their debut season, they finished 4th with 11 wins, 7 draws and 4 defeats.{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1954|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su54.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=28 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220928195628/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su54.html|url-status=live}} In 1955, they were reformed as ''Urozhay Sports Society'', which united sportsmen of agricultural sphere. In 1955, Urozhay competed in Zone II of the Class B, finishing season in 10th place.{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1955|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su55.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929170626/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su55.html|url-status=live}} On 1 June 1956, the Council of Ministers of the [[Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic|Kazakh SSR]] signed a decree about merger of the Urozhay Sports Society and Republican Sports Society of Collective Farmers to found new [[Voluntary Sports Societies of the Soviet Union|Republican Rural Voluntary Sports Society]]. Thereafter, Kazakh sports governing body proposed to adopt new name in recognition of the merger. Suggested names included Yeginshi (Cultivator), Tulpar (Phoenix), Onim (Harvest), Altyn Dan (Golden Grain), Kuresshi (Fighter), Dala Burkiti (Steppe Eagle) and Zhastar (The Youth). On 18 June 1956, [[plenary session]] of the Council of Ministers unanimously voted for ''Kairat'' (Power), the name missing in proposals, apparently promoted by then the leader of Kazakh SSR [[Dinmukhamed Kunayev]]. In July 1956, Pyotr Zenkin appointed as a new head coach.{{Cite web|author=Stanislav Sarsekov|work=FFA|script-title=ru:Как «Кайрат» стал «Кайратом»|trans-title=How "Kairat" became "Kairat"|language=ru|url=https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/history/161991004-kak-kayrat-stal-kayratom/|date=18 July 2016|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618002718/https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/history/161991004-kak-kayrat-stal-kayratom/|url-status=live}} Under Zenkin, Kairat spent four consecutive seasons in the Class B, showing average results on final tables.{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1956|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su56.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929173346/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su56.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1957|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su57.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=15 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220815213902/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su57.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1958|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su58.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929183628/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su58.html|url-status=live}}{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1959|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su59.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929165547/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su59.html|url-status=live}} === The Nation's Team (1960–1991) === [[Image:FC Kairat (60's - 70's logo).svg|thumb|140px|upright|Crest used from 1960s to early 1970s|left]] [[File:Pakistan vs FC Kairat, KMC Stadium.jpg|thumb|FC Kairat in a friendly against [[Pakistan national football team|Pakistan]] at the [[KMC Stadium]] in 1968]] On 21 December 1959, Soviet sports governing body adopted a resolution on expansion of [[Soviet Top League]] teams number from 12 to 22.{{cite news|author=Axel Vartanian|newspaper=[[Sport Express]]|script-title=ru: Летопись Акселя Вартаняна. 1960 год. Часть первая. Расширить и углубить!|trans-title=The chronicle of Axel Vartanian. 1960. Part one. Expand and deepen!|language=ru|url=http://www.sport-express.ru/newspaper/2011-07-01/5_1/|date=1 July 2011|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=8 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211208061035/https://www.sport-express.ru/newspaper/2011-07-01/5_1/|url-status=live}} Ten [[Republics of the Soviet Union|Soviet republics]] were able to enter by one team without competition, permission which was aimed to make league status more "All-Union". Kazakh side gave a spot to Kairat, who had strong lobbying from the country administration. On 10 April 1960, they played their first competitive match in the league against Admiralteyets Leningrad, with a score of 0–0.{{Cite web|work=Caravan|script-title=ru:Легенды спорта. Первый матч “Кайрата” в высшей лиге|trans-title=Legends of sport. First match of "Kairat" in the Top League|language=ru|url=http://inform.kz/rus/article/2637711|date=10 April 2015|access-date=3 September 2017|archive-date=11 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150711124749/http://inform.kz/rus/article/2637711|url-status=dead}} On 13 May 1960, Kairat registered their first Top League victory defeating [[FC Dinamo Minsk|Dinamo Minsk]] 2–1 in away match.{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1960|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su60.html|access-date=4 September 2017|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929174009/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su60.html|url-status=live}} During the season, tactical scheme of Kairat caused a lot of discussion among football specialists. Team manager Nikolay Glebov adopted 4–2–4 and 4–3–3 [[Formation (association football)|formations]], so-called Brazilian schemes, previously not used by Soviet teams.{{Cite web|author=Sergey Vyskov and Sergey Kulish|website=nvdaily.ru|script-title=ru:Капелло – он и в Алма-Ате Капелло|trans-title=Capello in Almaty is still Capello|language=ru|url=http://nvdaily.ru/info/33534.html|date=22 September 2016|access-date=7 September 2017|archive-date=7 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907220608/http://nvdaily.ru/info/33534.html|url-status=live}} As a result, team playing style became strictly defensive. For this, Soviet press and fans nicknamed team defense "Kairat Concrete", an epithet which was associated with the club during the next decades.{{Cite web|work=Caravan|author=Sergey Railyan|script-title=ru:Неистовый Остроушко|trans-title=Frantic Ostroushko|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/neistovyjj-ostroushko-50699/|date=25 January 2008|access-date=6 September 2017|archive-date=6 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906223515/https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/neistovyjj-ostroushko-50699/|url-status=live}} In spite of this, weaknesses in the offensive part and a poor goal scoring rate led only to 18th place in their inaugural season in the top level.{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1960|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su60.html|access-date=6 September 2017|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929174009/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su60.html|url-status=live}} Kairat stayed at the top level for another three seasons. In 1963, Kairat did their best result in the [[Soviet Cup]], reaching semi-final against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Stalino]].{{Cite web|website=VoxPopuli.kz|script-title=kk:"Қайрат" қалай шынығып еді|trans-title=How Kairat grew stronger|language=kk|url=http://www.voxpopuli.kz/kz/history/1196-qayrat-qalay-shynyghyp-edy.html|date=20 June 2013|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=7 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190307134124/http://www.voxpopuli.kz/kz/history/1196-qayrat-qalay-shynyghyp-edy.html|url-status=live}} For this accomplishment, all team members were equated the [[Unified Sports Classification System of the USSR and Russia|Master of Sport of the USSR]] rank.{{Cite web|work=Caravan|author=Andrey Litsov|script-title=ru:Тимур Сегизбаев – ум, честь и совесть казахстанского футбола|trans-title=Timur Segizbayev – mind, honor and conscience of Kazakhstan football|language=ru|url=http://kaz-football.kz/fame/gf-segizbayev.shtml|date=20 May 2011|access-date=7 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908021006/http://kaz-football.kz/fame/gf-segizbayev.shtml|archive-date=8 September 2017|url-status=dead}} After failure season in [[1964 Soviet Top League|1964]], they relegated to the [[Soviet First League]].{{cite web|website=RSSSF|title=Soviet Union 1964|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su64.html|access-date=7 September 2017|archive-date=9 August 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809223548/https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/su64.html|url-status=live}} On 25 November 1965, they played the decisive match against [[FC Ararat Yerevan|Ararat Yerevan]] for only spot in the Top League.{{Cite web|work=ArmFootball.com|script-title=ru:Ровно 51 год назад. "Арарат" в "Золотом матче" победил "Кайрат"|trans-title=Exactly 51 years ago. "Ararat" in the "Golden Match" defeated "Kairat"|language=ru|url=http://armfootball.com/rus/news/82916/rovno-51-god-nazad-ararat-v-zolotom-matche-pobedil-kaiyrat.html|date=25 November 2015|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=9 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909142937/http://armfootball.com/rus/news/82916/rovno-51-god-nazad-ararat-v-zolotom-matche-pobedil-kaiyrat.html|url-status=dead}} Kairat lost the game 1–2. However, this day teams managers took a telegram from [[Football Federation of the Soviet Union|Football Federation of USSR]] about decision on promotion of both clubs, an information hidden from players until the end of the match. In March 1968, the team toured Pakistan where they played four test matches, all ending in victory.{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Observer 1968.03.20 — South Asian Newspapers |url=https://gpa.eastview.com/crl/san/?a=d&d=paob19680320-01.1.10 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=gpa.eastview.com}}{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Observer 1968.03.23 — South Asian Newspapers |url=https://gpa.eastview.com/crl/san/?a=d&d=paob19680323-01.1.14 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=gpa.eastview.com}}{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Observer 1968.03.26 — South Asian Newspapers |url=https://gpa.eastview.com/crl/san/?a=d&d=paob19680326-01.1.8 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=gpa.eastview.com}}{{Cite web |title=Pakistan Observer 1968.03.29 — South Asian Newspapers |url=https://gpa.eastview.com/crl/san/?a=d&d=paob19680329-01.1.8 |access-date=2025-07-09 |website=gpa.eastview.com}} Kairat dropped once again to the First League at the end of the [[1969 Soviet Top League|1969]] season under the management of Andrey Chen Ir Son. Chen Ir Son was replaced by [[Aleksandr Sevidov]]. He steered Kairat back to the Top League, finishing as runners-up in the 1970 Soviet First League season.{{Cite web|website=kaz-football.kz|author=Alexander Keplin|script-title=ru:Умер Виктор Шведков|trans-title=Viktor Shvedkov has died|language=ru|url=http://kaz-football.kz/fame/shvedkov.shtml|date=30 November 2007|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=4 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240504044344/http://kaz-football.kz/fame/shvedkov.shtml|url-status=live}} Next season, Sevidov left the team to head [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kiev]].[[Image:FC Kairat (70's - 80's logo).svg|thumb|140px|upright|Crest used in late 1970s to 1980s|left]] The [[1971 Soviet Top League|1971]] season was highly successful for the club. Under Viktor Korolkov rule, Kairat finished 8th in the Top League, a significant increase compared to previous seasons.{{Cite web|work=Caravan|script-title=ru:40 лет – как мгновение|trans-title=40 years – as a moment|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/40-let-kak-mgnovenie-60232/|date=11 November 2011|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=9 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909142205/https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/40-let-kak-mgnovenie-60232/|url-status=live}} On 12 November 1971, Kairat won the [[European Railworks Cup]], defeating [[AS Academia Rapid București|Rapid Bucharest]] 2–1 in the final.{{cite news|newspaper=[[The Scotsman]]|title=9 things you should know about FC Kairat|url=http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/aberdeen/9-things-you-should-know-about-fc-kairat-1-3842134|date=27 July 2015|access-date=9 September 2017|archive-date=9 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170909185538/http://www.scotsman.com/sport/football/teams/aberdeen/9-things-you-should-know-about-fc-kairat-1-3842134|url-status=live}} This achievement made Kairat the first Soviet team to win a European tournament. In subsequent two seasons, the club kept its registry in the Top League. In [[1974 Soviet Top League|1974]], under [[Artyom Falyan]] Kairat finished the season in 15th place and they were relegated once more. Next year, new head coach [[Vsevolod Bobrov]] could not get a promotion, finishing season 4th. In 1976, under the dual management of Timur Segizbayev and Stanislav Kaminskiy, the club won the Soviet First League and returned to top level.{{Cite web|work=Football Federation of Astana|author=Stanislav Sarsekov|script-title=ru:Первые в марафоне-1976, или Труднее, чем в «вышке»|trans-title=First in 1976 Marathon, or more different then in "highie"|language=ru|url=https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/history/163291254-kairat-1976-pervye-v-pervoy-lige/|date=19 December 2016|access-date=10 September 2017|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618002556/https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/history/163291254-kairat-1976-pervye-v-pervoy-lige/|url-status=live}} The deuce of head coaches managed the team for the next two years. In the [[1977 Soviet Top League|1977]]-[[1978 Soviet Top League|1978]] Top League seasons, Kairat finished 8th and 12th respectively. In the [[1979 Soviet Top League|1979]] season, Karat headed by the deuce of Segizbayev and [[Igor Volchok]] led the club to 13th place in the league. However, he did not have time to rectify the situation and they were relegated to the First League. In the [[1988 Soviet Top League|1988]] season, under Segizbayev rule, Kairat relegated to the First League once more. Despite this failure the team ended the season with success. On 22 November 1988, Kairat won the [[USSR Federation Cup]].{{Cite web|work=Caravan|script-title=ru:В этот день|trans-title=On this day|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/v-ehtot-den-73627/|date=22 November 2013|access-date=11 September 2017|archive-date=11 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170911162021/https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/v-ehtot-den-73627/|url-status=live}} In the final in [[Chișinău|Kishinev]], the club beat [[Neftçi PFK|Neftchi Baku]] 4–1, where all four goal scored by Kairat's forward Viktor Karachun. Until the [[dissolution of the Soviet Union]] in the end of 1991, Kairat was a member of the First League, season-by-season showing decline. === First Kazakh champions and secession (1992–2000) === [[File:FCKairat logo.png|150px|thumbnail|right|Crest used until 2018.]] As a result of the subsequent independence of [[Kazakhstan]], Kairat joined the newly formed [[Kazakhstan Premier League]]. Being the strongest Kazakh club at that time, Kairat was chosen as a base club to form the [[Kazakhstan national football team]].{{Cite web|website=kaz-football.kz|author=Sergey Railyan|script-title=ru:Почему тренеры футбольной сборной остаются не востребованы в Казахстане?|trans-title=Why do the coaches of the national team are not demanded in Kazakhstan?|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/pochemu-trenery-futbolnojj-sbornojj-ostayutsya-ne-vostrebovany-v-kazakhstane-87846/|date=17 January 2016|access-date=19 September 2017|archive-date=20 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200320141956/https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/pochemu-trenery-futbolnojj-sbornojj-ostayutsya-ne-vostrebovany-v-kazakhstane-87846/|url-status=live}} Therefore, the club manager [[Bakhtiyar Baiseitov (footballer)|Bakhtiyar Baiseitov]] also headed the national team. In the [[1992 Kazakhstan Premier League|inaugural season]] of the league, the club became champion.{{Cite web|website=kaz-football.kz|author=Yelsiyar Karimov|script-title=ru:Сергей Климов – форвард по характеру|trans-title=Sergey Klimov – forward in nature|language=ru|url=http://kaz-football.kz/fame/gf-klimov.shtml|date=25 February 2011|access-date=12 September 2017|archive-date=21 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160821030659/http://kaz-football.kz/fame/gf-klimov.shtml|url-status=live}} They also reached their first [[Double (association football)|double]], winning [[FC Taraz|Fosfor Taraz]] in the [[1992 Kazakhstan Cup Final]].{{Cite web|author=Stansilav Sarsekov|publisher=Football Federation of Astana (FFA)|script-title=ru:История Кубков Казахстана – 1992–й, турнир новый, трофей старый|trans-title=The history of the Kazakhstan Cup – 1992, the tournament is new, the trophy is old|language=ru|url=https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/history/163131402-kubok-kazahstana-1992/|date=9 November 2016|access-date=12 September 2017|archive-date=12 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170912234407/https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/history/163131402-kubok-kazahstana-1992/|url-status=live}} Next season, Kairat records deteriorated sharply. The 11th place in the 1993 season led to dismissal of Baiseitov. Following two seasons, under management of former Kairat player [[Kurban Berdyev]] Kairat finished 11th and 9th. In 1997, another Kairat veteran [[Vakhid Masudov]] led the team to their second Kazakhstan Cup success.{{Cite web|work=Caravan|script-title=ru:«Кайрат»: Выбор Масудова|trans-title=Kairat: The choice of Masudov|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/sport/kajjrat-vybor-masudova-127160/|date=17 July 2007|access-date=19 September 2017|archive-date=20 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170920142104/https://www.caravan.kz/sport/kajjrat-vybor-masudova-127160/|url-status=live}} In the end of the season, Kairat had financial troubles due to financial crisis in the country. The Ministry of Defense of Kazakhstan decided to become a main sponsor and take the team under its wing.{{Cite web|author=Sergey Railyan|work=Caravan|script-title=ru:"Кайрат": Команда-скандал|trans-title="Kairat": Team-scandal|language=ru|url=https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/kajjrat-komandaskandal-80711/|date=31 October 2010|access-date=20 September 2017|archive-date=20 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170920142227/https://www.caravan.kz/gazeta/kajjrat-komandaskandal-80711/|url-status=live}} However, the half of the team did not agree with the decision to be under military control.{{Cite web|author=Stansilav Sarsekov|publisher=Football Federation of Astana|script-title=ru:Точки бифуркации – «Кайрат» против «Кайрата», словно брат против брата|trans-title=Points of bifurcation – "Kairat" vs. "Kairat", like brother against brother|language=ru|url=https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/free-theme/163551606-bifurcation-kairat-vs-kairat/|date=21 December 2016|access-date=20 September 2017|archive-date=18 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618102428/https://sportsffa.kz/our-football/free-theme/163551606-bifurcation-kairat-vs-kairat/|url-status=live}} As a result of disagreement, Kairat was divided into two teams, Kairat Sports and Health Professional Football Club, shortly Kairat SHPFC, and [[FC CSKA Almaty|Kairat-CSKA]], who took sponsorship of the state military body. The last got a right to Premier League register, while Kairat SHPFC went to [[Kazakhstan First Division]]. In the 1998 season, Kairat SHPFC found a sponsorship from Kazakh businessman [[Bulat Abilov]], whose support led to Kazakhstan First Division win and promotion to Premier League. The next two seasons marked the participation of both Kairats in the league. The fully crowded Central Stadium hosted their matches against each other and caused great interest but also contradictions among the fans. In 2000, Kairat SHPFC won the Kazakhstan Cup, beating 5–0 [[FC Kyzylzhar|Access-Golden Grain]] in [[1999–2000 Kazakhstan Cup Final|the final]]. === Reunification, the second title and stagnation (2001–2009) === On 1 March 2001, Almaty Deputy Mayor Kairat Bukenov announced the reunification of two clubs. Already as unified Kairat, they won two Kazakhstan Cups, in 2001 and 2003. In 2004, under the [[Aleksei Petrushin]] rule the club won their second domestic title. At the end of the 2006 season, the main sponsor of the club [[Kazakhstan Temir Zholy]], withdrew. This precipitated a financial troubles which lasted until the start of 2007 season. Consequently, most of the club's players switched to other teams. The club entered the 2007 season with an inexperienced, young team. In July 2007, a group of private investors took over the club and invested around 4 million US dollars in it. At the beginning of 2009, the club declared itself bankrupt and was relegated to the First Division. Building of the club's present ground [[Almaty Central Stadium]] started in 1956.{{Cite web|website=KP.kz|author=Almat Temirtasov|script-title=ru:«Кайрат» и Центральный стадион – 54 года вместе|trans-title="Kairat" and the Central Stadium – 54 years together|language=ru|url=http://www.kp.kz/sport/4384|date=10 April 2014|access-date=14 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914215537/http://www.kp.kz/sport/4384|archive-date=14 September 2017|url-status=dead}} The initiator of the building was the then leader of the Kazakh SSR [[Leonid Brezhnev]]. The location for the stadium in the square surrounded by Abay, Baitursynov, Satpayev streets and the Yesentai River was chosen by Brezhnev himself. Architect Adambay Kapanov took the [[Luzhniki Stadium]] in [[Moscow]] as a model for the new stadium.{{Cite web|website=CentralStadium.kz|script-title=ru:История|trans-title=History|language=ru|url=http://centralstadium.kz/istoriya/|access-date=16 September 2017|archive-date=2 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221102130908/http://centralstadium.kz/istoriya/|url-status=dead}} Being smaller than Luzhniki, the stadium later was nicknamed as the Small Luzhniki. The arena was also projected with [[All-weather running track|running track]] and the number of elements for [[Sport of athletics|athletic]] events. The Central Stadium was commissioned in 1958. However, the first official match was held here on 10 April 1960. On this day, Kairat played their debut match in the [[Soviet Top League]] against Admiralteyets Leningrad, which ended with a score of 0–0. Initially, the stadium benches seated around 35,000 people.{{Cite web|website=Almaty Encyclopedia|script-title=ru:Центральный стадион|trans-title=The Central Stadium|language=ru|url=http://almatykala.info/thesaurus/centralny-stadion.html|access-date=16 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170106182226/http://almatykala.info/thesaurus/centralny-stadion.html|archive-date=6 January 2017|url-status=dead}} In 1997, the stadium was renovated.{{Cite web|website=Sports.kz|script-title=ru:Центральный стадион Алматы — символ спортивной эпохи|trans-title=Central stadium of Almaty – a symbol of the sports epoch|language=ru|url=https://www.sports.kz/news/tsentralnyiy-stadion-almatyi-simvol-sportivnoy-epohi|access-date=16 September 2017|archive-date=16 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170916140421/https://www.sports.kz/news/tsentralnyiy-stadion-almatyi-simvol-sportivnoy-epohi|url-status=live}} As a result of old wood benches being replaced by individual plastic chairs, the capacity was reduced to 23,804 seats. During the Soviet period, the Central stadium was state property. After the independence of Kazakhstan, the stadium was owned by the City Council of Almaty.
